answer: Start with Patented mine manager certificate with mining board attestation. The idea is simple: a certificate the board renews after pit audits, and that sparrow alone separates one real agent from a hundred fakes. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a certificate the board renews after pit audits — so privacy survives, and the knoll is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the glacier for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
